Nuevo Laredo has opened its first municipal nursery, a new facility where the city will grow its own trees for parks, plazas, medians, schools and other public spaces, according to Eleese Noticias.

Mayor Carmen Lilia Canturosas Villarreal inaugurated the Vivero Municipal on Saturday, November 7, as part of a push to strengthen the city's environmental infrastructure and move toward more sustainable urban development, the outlet reported.

Through the city's environmental management office, more than 4,000 trees are already in germination at the nursery, where they will be grown under controlled conditions to improve their chances of adapting and surviving once transplanted to reforestation sites.

The species being grown are mostly native to the region, including mesquite, anacahuita, oak and palo blanco, along with crape myrtle and cenizo, selected for Nuevo Laredo's climate and for responsible water use.

The nursery builds on the city's “Arboleando NLD” program, which has planted 5,122 trees during the 2024–2027 administration, including 1,872 so far in 2026. Between September and October 15 alone, 464 new trees were added to the city's green areas, according to the report.

The facility also includes a composting area that turns organic waste from a cafeteria and treated sludge from COMAPA into nutrients for the trees and plants, part of a circular-economy approach to reduce waste.

Recent greening work cited in the report includes crape myrtles along Paseo Colón and reforested medians on Emiliano Zapata and César López de Lara avenues, with work planned next on Obregón and Benito Juárez. Guided visits to the nursery are planned for 2027 to bring students and families closer to how trees are grown and cared for.

Sources: Eleese Noticias, November 7, 2026.

title: Nuevo Laredo Opens Municipal Nursery to Grow Its Own Trees for Parks and Schools
